title: OpenAI-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: This PR updates the OpenAI compatibility layer to (1) implement tool_choice semantics for assistant decisions, (2) add schema mapping utilities so Redwood tool schemas map cleanly to OpenAI-style tool JSON schemas, and (3) standardize tool message formatting emitted into chats and event logs. Motivation: A number of downstream customers and SDKs expect OpenAI-style tool calling behavior (tool_choice, structured 'tool' messages, and schema validation) for interoperability. Previously our compatibility layer returned a lightweight 'invoke_tool' event which lacked explicit tool_choice metadata and did not consistently emit tool messages that matched the OpenAI shapes. This caused issues with SDKs and third-party integrations that rely on tool metadata and schema validation. Changes implemented: - tool_choice: adds an explicit top-level field in assistant responses within the compat layer ("tool_choice"): when the model decides to call a tool, we surface the chosen tool id, the reason_str (short rationale), and a canonical argument payload (stringified JSON). This follows OpenAI semantics: the client can rely on tool_choice to decide to call a tool without re-parsing free-form assistant text. - schema mapping: a new util (openai_compat.schema_mapper) maps Redwood tool parameter specs (typed shapes, enums, nested objects) -> OpenAI-style JSON Schema. Mapping supports required/optional, enums, string/number/boolean types, array/item schemas, and nested objects. We add defensive guards for unsupported types and log a mapping hint so operators can resolve schema mismatches. - tool message formatting: standardizes assistant tool-invocation messages to follow the OpenAI message format: role="tool" name=<tool_id> content=<serialized args>. Also updates event logs and audit entries to include both the parsed args object (for internal tooling) and the original serialized payload (for fidelity). - streaming stability: fixes a race in the streaming layer where a mid-stream tool_choice event could be emitted twice when the model partials included both a tool token and a follow-up assistant token. The fix introduces a small merge window and a deterministic emitter that coalesces partial events into a single tool message. - backward compatibility: compat layer will still accept older-style 'invoke_tool' events for a short deprecation window and converts them to the new tool_choice+tool message shape. Migration guide and SDK examples are included in docs. Checklist: - [x] Implement tool_choice semantics in compat layer - [x] Add schema mapping util and tests - [x] Standardize tool message formatting and update event logs - [x] Streaming race fix and unit/integration tests - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] E2E test with python/ts SDKs Testing: unit tests cover schema mapper (edge cases for arrays and nested objects), tool message emitter (stream/dedup scenarios), and conversion from legacy invoke_tool events. Integration tests run against the redwood-compat test harness using model simulator v2. CI: full test matrix passed (unit, integration, lint). Impact: No breaking change for existing users in the short term; new behavior provides a clearer contract for SDKs adopting OpenAI semantics. Operators should review schema mapping logs for any unsupported tool parameter types. Rollout: merged to main with feature flag openai_compat.tool_choice enabled for 10% of requests initially, then widened after monitoring.

release_notes: Adds OpenAI-compatible tool_choice semantics and schema mapping utilities. Standardizes tool message formatting in the compatibility layer and fixes a streaming duplicate emission race. Backwards-compatible conversion of legacy invoke_tool events is included. See docs/openai-compat.md for migration steps.
